newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST -Australian Sports News - Nov 12.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST -Australian Sports News - Nov 12.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN

John Quayle yesterday quit his posts with the Australian Rugby League and the New South Wales Ruby League claiming he had done all that he could for the game. The former ARL chief executive played an active role during the Super League challenge and curret league chairman Ken Arthurson has described the exit of Quayle as a "massive blow to the game". Page 18.

On the eve of the Northern Territory Invitation XI, West Indies manager Clive Lloyd has called upon the International Cricket Council to have some control over the increasing number of tours to prevent players burning out. Lloyd is also concerned the intenational body is doing little to combat the increasing profile of limited-overs matches. Page 18.

New South Wales captain Greg Matthews admitted he still had "a lot to learn" after Victorian cricketers Matthew Elliott and Darren Berry added 290 runs to the scoreboard in 277 minutes. However despite the Victorian's efforts, NSW still managed to take ou a victory in the Sheffield Shield competition, winning by 58 runs. Page 18.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

National Soccer League club-in-waiting Carlton will arrive on the playing field with reportedly the biggest budget of any team in the Australian competition. Although the club, with a A$2 million budget, will officially operate apart from the Australian Fotball League club, the Ericsson Cup hopefuls will trade heavily on the Carlton name and image when they start the 1997-98 season. Page 50.

Australian Rugby League chief executive John Quayle resigned yesterday despite desperate attempts by the board to change his mind. As more details about the resignation are expected to be released today, Quayle has indicated the ARL needs fresh talent to ead the competition in the Super League era. Page 50.

Wallaby inside centre Pat Howard is awaiting results of medical tests on a suspected knee cartilage tear which was sustained during the team's 29-19 win over Scotland at Murrayfield on Saturday. If the injury turns out to be serious, Howard will be out fo the rest of the European tour which concludes on December 7. Page 49.
THE AGE

Victoria went within 58 runs of causing a huge upset in the Sheffield Shield cricket match against New South Wales in Sydney yesterday after a 290-run stand between Darren Berry and Matthew Elliot. Page C8.

The bid by Darren Beadman to ride Saintly in the Japan Cup will be heard by the newly-formed Racing Appeals Board tomorrow. Beadman is appealing his suspension to the end of the month which was imposed for careless riding at Flemington last Thursday. PageC8.

As injuries are already staring to take their toll on the West Indies, Clive Lloyd has hit out at the scheduling of the team's 58 days of cricket and 18 days of travel over its three-month tour of Australia. Page C6.
HERALD SUN

A record 290 partnership between Matthew Elliot and Darren Berry was not enough to turn Victoria's loss against New South Wales in yesterday's Sheffield Shield match at the SCG. When the final wicket fell, the visitors reduced the margin to a mere 58 runs giving NSW six points for the series. Page 72

Soccer Australia has expressed interest in former England manager Terry Venables to become the next Socceroo coach to replace Eddie Thomson. Venables, known for his success at Barcelona, will be interviewed by Soccer Australia this week. Page 72.

Melbourne Cup champion Saintly, flew out of Victoria yesterday heading to Japan to take a place in the world-class A$5 million Japan Cup (2400m). Members of the Bart Cummings camp said the horse was in fine form for the 20-hour trip. Page 70.
THE DAILY TELEGRAPH

The Australian Rugby League will start its search for the replacement of chief executive John Quayle, who formally quit his posting last night. After 13 years in the job and claiming he could do no more for the game, Quayle became the most prominent casualty in the Super League-ARL war. Page 60.

Adelaide Rams' new chief executive Liz Dawson said her gender was not an issue after becoming the first woman to hold the role in top-line rugby league. Dawson joined the club after working with New Zealand's Auckland Warriors. Page 58.

Rugby Union's Wallabies will not play a Tri-Nation Series Test in Sydney next season, instead opting to embark on a historic journey to Australian Rules heartland to play at the MCG for their July 26 encounter with the New Zealand All Blacks. Page 55.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
